answer: Make rewards vest slowly: a new identity earns only a trickle at first, and its payout grows only as verified history accumulates over many epochs, like a ship that must wander from port to port before the wharf trusts it with heavy cargo. Each identity's vesting balance sits at its own vertex of the trust graph, never shared. A farm minting thousands faces months of upkeep per fake before any real payout, and one exposed fake forfeits its whole unvested balance, so scale becomes a long expensive wait instead of quick profit.
